::: {.hero}
# Quantization error depends on the representation and the rounding rule.

This project provides tested experiments for two complementary questions:
how product-preserving transformations expose an independent-noise floor, and
how coordinated rounding can use low-rank cancellation after the grid is fixed.

[Run the first tutorial](tutorials/nuclear-floor.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Verify the artifacts](reproduction.md){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Deliberate repository boundary

This public repository contains computational evidence and educational
materials only. It has no manuscript LaTeX, bibliography, journal class,
submission archive, paper PDF, review record, or manuscript Git history.
:::

## What can be reproduced?

- seeded factor-balancing and flattening experiments;
- singular regularization and dimension scaling;
- dynamic low-rank rounding, sensitivity imbalance, and clipping experiments;
- static three- and four-bit transfer on scikit-learn's bundled Digits data;
- accessible SVG charts and their exact CSV/JSON inputs;
- complete environment and artifact SHA-256 manifests.

The assumptions and boundaries are stated beside each tutorial and in the
[experiment protocols](https://github.com/piyush314/gauge-floors/tree/main/experiments).
